lessons.title: Put invariants in the schema
lessons.body:
### A table can reject invalid data
PRIMARY KEY identifies a row. UNIQUE prevents duplicate key values according to the constraint’s null semantics. NOT NULL requires a value. CHECK enforces a predicate.

```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts (
 id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
 balance INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (balance >= 0)
);
```

Choose integer minor units for simple money examples. A production financial model needs additional currency and precision decisions.

lessons.title: Commit related changes together
lessons.body:
### Treat a transfer as one operation
A debit and a credit belong in one transaction. BEGIN starts a transaction; COMMIT makes its changes durable within the database; ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes.

### Think about failures
If a constraint violation aborts a PostgreSQL transaction, roll back before continuing. A transaction protects related changes, but business validation still matters.

In this lab, the database is in memory. A commit does not make it survive a browser reload.

exercises.title: Transfer without losing money
exercises.prompt: Move 30 units from account 1 to account 2 in a single transaction. Verify the final balances and the unchanged total. Load the exercise data first. If your transaction fails, run ROLLBACK before retrying.
hints: Wrap both updates with BEGIN and COMMIT.
